data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: PHYSICAL SECURITY STANDARDS FOR INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) RESTRICTED SPACE

actors.name: individual who has knowledge of the system being worked on
Associate CIO for Information Resources Management (IRM)
Agency Managers for IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Web Farms, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) and Isolation Zones
agency Information System Security Program Managers/staff
law enforcement and other investigative personnel
personnel having an ongoing recurring business need
Personnel who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space
Agency Information System Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: The United States Department of Agriculture houses and processes information relating to the privacy of US citizens, payroll and financial transactions, proprietary information and life/mission critical data.
policy_statements.target: information relating to the privacy of US citizens, payroll and financial transactions, proprietary information and life/mission critical data

policy_statements.source_text: It is essential that this information be protected from the risk and magnitude of loss or harm that could result from inadvertent or deliberate disclosure, alteration or destruction.
USDA must protect information resources through layered physical security, high logical data security and effective security procedures and administration.
Successful IT security protection dictates the physical control of restricted space that contains major USDA computer and telecommunications resources.
policy_statements.target: physical control of restricted space that contains major USDA computer and telecommunications resources

policy_statements.source_text: The purpose of this chapter is to define the physical security standards for all IT equipment/devices in this space.
policy_statements.target: physical security standards for all IT equipment/devices in this space

policy_statements.source_text: Many USDA facilities house highly sensitive critical IT infrastructure components.
policy_statements.target: highly sensitive critical IT infrastructure components

policy_statements.source_text: As such, it is essential that every precaution be used to safeguard this information capability.
Information technology infrastructures will be housed in IT Restricted Space that meets the requirements of the physical security standards outlined below.
conditions: that meets the requirements of the physical security standards outlined below

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA agencies are responsible for coordinating the physical security requirements of their critical infrastructure resources.
policy_statements.target: physical security requirements of their critical infrastructure resources

policy_statements.source_text: Specifically, agencies are responsible for coordinating the physical security requirements of all IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Telecommunications/Local Area Network (LAN) Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones.
policy_statements.target: physical security requirements of all IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Telecommunications/Local Area Network (LAN) Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones

policy_statements.source_text: These standards apply to existing and planned space to be utilized for this purpose.
policy_statements.target: existing and planned space to be utilized for this purpose
conditions: to be utilized for this purpose

policy_statements.source_text: While every IT facility may not meet the physical security standards outlined above, CS will work with the agency, functional business owner and others to develop acceptable short and long term mitigation strategies to meet the needs of the Department.
policy_statements.target: acceptable short and long term mitigation strategies
conditions: While every IT facility may not meet the physical security standards outlined above

policy_statements.source_text: IT Restricted Space will be controlled directly by USDA personnel who will have the ultimate responsibility for control of these areas.
All IT Restricted Space will have a facility based Occupant Emergency Plan.

New or planned specifications for IT Restricted Space will contain a provision that the physical security requirements will be coordinated with Cyber Security far enough in advance during the design phase to ensure compliance with this policy.
policy_statements.target: New or planned specifications for IT Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: Pending revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) to include security requirements, all agencies will include physical security requirements in all Statements of Work (SOW) and Procurement Requests for IT Restricted Space.
conditions: Pending revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) to include security requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies will submit all policy exception requests directly to the ACIO for Cyber Security.
Exceptions to policy will be considered only in terms of implementation timeframes; exceptions will not be granted to the requirement to conform to this policy.
conditions: only in terms of implementation timeframes

policy_statements.source_text: Exceptions that are approved will be interim in nature and will require that each agency report this Granted Policy Exception (GPE) as a Plan of Action & Milestone (POA&M) in their FISMA reporting, with a GPE notation, until full compliance is achieved.
conditions: that are approved
until full compliance is achieved

policy_statements.source_text: Interim exceptions expire with each fiscal year.
conditions: with each fiscal year

policy_statements.source_text: Compliance exceptions that require longer durations will be renewed on an annual basis with a updated timeline for completion.
policy_statements.target: Compliance exceptions that require longer durations
conditions: that require longer durations
on an annual basis with a updated timeline for completion

policy_statements.source_text: CS will monitor all approved exceptions.
The Critical Infrastructure consists of those physical and cyber-based systems essential to the minimum operations of the economy and government.
They include, but are not limited to, telecommunications, energy, banking and finance, transportation, water systems and emergency services, both governmental and private.
Many of the nation’s critical infrastructures have been physically and logically separate systems that have little interdependence.
This is also true in the case of USDA’s Critical Infrastructure, which is managed collectively under different programs in the department.
The goals of these programs are diverse and not always overlapping in their security efforts.

USDA buildings that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment automatically are considered critical IT Infrastructure Restricted Space and USDA must provide a level of physical security commensurate with that designation.
policy_statements.target: USDA buildings that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment
conditions: that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Devices, in these facilities, which process or access sensitive data on a recurring basis will be protected in accordance with minimum security protection standards.
conditions: which process or access sensitive data on a recurring basis

policy_statements.source_text: IT Restricted Space areas must be secured in accordance with the requirements specified below:
General Facility Security Requirements

Physical security for this space will be provided in compliance with the recommendations established for Federal Facilities by the Department of Justice, Vulnerability Assessment, dated June 28, 1995.
cross_references: Department of Justice, Vulnerability Assessment, dated June 28, 1995

policy_statements.source_text: Parking: Facility parking will be controlled; signs will be posted and arrangements will be made for towing of unauthorized vehicles; adequate lighting will be provided for parking areas;
Closed Circuit Television (CCTV): CCTV surveillance cameras with time-lapse video recording will be provided;
policy_statements.target: CCTV surveillance cameras with time-lapse video recording

policy_statements.source_text: Lighting: Lighting with emergency power backup will be provided;
Access Control: Facility will be controlled by armed security guards and an intrusion detection system with central monitoring capability maintained to current life safety standards;
Entrances/Exits: High security locks will be installed and used;
Employee/Visitor Identification: Agency photo ID will be required for all personnel and ID will be displayed at all times; visitors will be controlled and screened;
Utilities: Utility access will be restricted to authorized personnel; emergency power will be provided to all critical systems (alarms, radio communications, computer facilities, etc.);
Occupant Emergency Plans (OEP): OEPs will be implemented in facilities, updated and tested annually;
Training: Annual Security Awareness Training will be conducted.
General IT Restrictions -
Prior to the determination of a IT Restricted Space location, consideration will be given to its proximity to public areas.
conditions: Prior to the determination of a IT Restricted Space location

policy_statements.source_text: Public areas are defined as areas that are maintained for or can be used by the public or the general community, such as rest rooms, libraries or visitor centers.
IT Restricted Space should not be located either above, adjacent, or below public areas in multi-story buildings;
All packages being delivered to the IT Restricted Space will be x-rayed first.
policy_statements.target: All packages being delivered to the IT Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: All mail/packages must be recorded in a log book;

Periodic inspections of the door locking mechanism will be conducted by agency IT personnel on a bi-annual basis to provide assurance that hardware cannot be easily manipulated to gain unauthorized access;
policy_statements.target: Periodic inspections of the door locking mechanism
conditions: on a bi-annual basis

policy_statements.source_text: The roving guard will periodically inspect IT Restricted Space entrances for signs of forced entry; and
Signage indicating IT Restricted Space locations is prohibited.
policy_statements.target: Signage indicating IT Restricted Space locations

policy_statements.source_text: Physical Security Standards for IT Restricted Space -
The IT Restricted Space will be located in the interior of the building away from exterior windows, if practical;
conditions: if practical

policy_statements.source_text: If floor plans are used at entrances to identify locations within the facility, critical asset locations will not be identified;
conditions: If floor plans are used at entrances to identify locations within the facility

policy_statements.source_text: Wall construction of the IT Restricted Space will be slab-to-slab with Sound Transmission Class 40 or better and other criteria cited in the ISC Security Design Criteria for Federal Buildings;
policy_statements.target: Wall construction of the IT Restricted Space
cross_references: ISC Security Design Criteria for Federal Buildings

policy_statements.source_text: The computer room will be protected by a fire suppressant system in accordance with local fire code, preferably dry-pipe;
Entrances to the IT Restricted Space will be kept to the minimum required by local fire code;
policy_statements.target: Entrances to the IT Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: Activities with visitor populations will be located a minimum of 50 feet from IT Restricted Space ;
Mailrooms will not be located within 50 feet of IT Restricted Space and cannot be placed over or under this space;
Storage areas and loading docks will not be located within 50 feet of IT Restricted Space and cannot be placed over or under this space;
Glass doors or windows will not be used in IT Restricted Space;
Metal clad doors or solid wood doors with a 2-hour fire rating will be used at all IT Restricted Space entrances;
policy_statements.target: Metal clad doors or solid wood doors with a 2-hour fire rating

policy_statements.source_text: Entrance to the computer room will be via electronic access control with the capability of providing an audit trail; Biometric Systems are encouraged;
Exterior computer room doors having key access hardware will be removed from the Master Key system of the facility;
policy_statements.target: Exterior computer room doors having key access hardware
conditions: having key access hardware

policy_statements.source_text: The issuance of non-Master Keys must be controlled only to individuals with an ongoing business need;
conditions: only to individuals with an ongoing business need

policy_statements.source_text: An intrusion detection system will be installed on all computer room entrances;
The access control and intrusion detection systems will have Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) backup;
policy_statements.target: access control and intrusion detection systems

policy_statements.source_text: Exterior IT Restricted Space doors will have either interior hinges or exterior hinges with non-removable pins;
Based on the determination of mission criticality by each agency, computer rooms and web farms will have back-up generators and UPS;
conditions: Based on the determination of mission criticality by each agency

policy_statements.source_text: Weapons are not allowed in IT Restricted space with the exception of armed security officers, law enforcement and other investigative personnel; and
conditions: with the exception of armed security officers, law enforcement and other investigative personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Backup tapes that contain mission critical or sensitive information will be stored offsite.
policy_statements.target: Backup tapes that contain mission critical or sensitive information
conditions: that contain mission critical or sensitive information

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel Security Requirements -
Only personnel having an ongoing recurring business need will be given unescorted access to the IT Restricted Space;
policy_statements.target: personnel having an ongoing recurring business need
conditions: having an ongoing recurring business need

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space will immediately be removed from the access control system;
policy_statements.target: Personnel who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space
conditions: who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: Visitors should be kept to a bare minimum; tours by non-USDA personnel are prohibited;

A sign in/sign out logbook shall be required for all escorted visitors; as a minimum the logbook shall contain the printed identity of each visitor, visitor’s signature, agency/company represented, purpose of visit, date/time in and date/time out;
Cleaning and maintenance personnel shall be escorted at all times by USDA or permanent contractor personnel;
An individual who has knowledge of the system being worked on shall escort non-permanent contractors needing access to the IT Restricted Space at all times; and
policy_statements.actor_name: individual who has knowledge of the system being worked on
policy_statements.target: non-permanent contractors needing access to the IT Restricted Space
conditions: who has knowledge of the system being worked on
needing access to the IT Restricted Space
at all times

policy_statements.source_text: A quarterly access review by the agency will be conducted of designated personnel (i.e., maintenance) having an ongoing business need in all restricted space.
policy_statements.target: designated personnel (i.e., maintenance) having an ongoing business need in all restricted space
conditions: having an ongoing business need in all restricted space

policy_statements.source_text: Web Farm Restricted Requirements
Web Farms located in rooms other than a secure computing facility will be subject to the same physical security requirements outlined above; sections a-d above apply; and
policy_statements.target: Web Farms located in rooms other than a secure computing facility
conditions: located in rooms other than a secure computing facility

policy_statements.source_text: The room must have Web Farm computing equipment contained in secured cabinets.
The Chief Information Officer/Deputy will:
Promote and support effective physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space.
policy_statements.target: effective physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: The Associate CIO for Cyber Security will:

Publish physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space, to include Computer Facilities, Web Farms, Telecommunications/Magnetic Media Rooms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones ;
policy_statements.target: physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: Actively participate in the planning and design of all new IT Restricted Space to ensure that IT physical security standards are incorporated in space layouts for offices, buildings and complexes;
policy_statements.target: planning and design of all new IT Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct on-site reviews of all existing IT Restricted Space to ensure that all Mission Critical, Departmental Priority and Sensitive Systems are protected through adequate layered physical security;
Provide subject matter expert advice to USDA agencies on physical security standards as they relate to IT Restricted Space; and
Review all exception requests concerning compliance time limit extensions or alternate methods of mitigating physical security risks by USDA agencies as they relate to IT Restricted Space.
policy_statements.target: all exception requests concerning compliance time limit extensions or alternate methods of mitigating physical security risks by USDA agencies as they relate to IT Restricted Space

policy_statements.source_text: The Associate CIO for Information Resources Management (IRM) will:
Support exception requests from the policy and procedures contained in this chapter to ensure that appropriate security protection is provided to all USDA IT Restricted Space; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Information Resources Management (IRM)
policy_statements.target: exception requests from the policy and procedures contained in this chapter

policy_statements.source_text: Receive, review and coordinate a response with the Associate CIO for Cyber Security.
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Information Resources Management (IRM)

policy_statements.source_text: The Agency Chief Information Officer will:
Ensure that all agency personnel, especially the Agency Information System Security Program Manager (ISSPM) are aware of the policy and procedures concerning Restricted IT Space;
Proactively consult with the Associate CIO for Cyber Security when planning or designing IT space in new buildings or space for the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure in an existing facility;
conditions: when planning or designing IT space in new buildings or space for the Information Technology (IT) infrastructure in an existing facility

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that reviews are conducted of all agency IT Restricted space to make certain that they comply with the physical security requirements of this manual within 120 days from issuance of this manual.
conditions: within 120 days from issuance of this manual

policy_statements.source_text: Facilities that contain mission critical, departmental priority or sensitive systems will be reviewed by OCIO at least annually for compliance with physical security requirements;
policy_statements.target: Facilities that contain mission critical, departmental priority or sensitive systems
conditions: that contain mission critical, departmental priority or sensitive systems
at least annually

policy_statements.source_text: Provide a written report of all IT Restricted Space facilities not in compliance with these requirements to the Associate CIO for Cyber Security within 150 days from issuance of this document;
policy_statements.target: written report of all IT Restricted Space facilities not in compliance with these requirements
conditions: within 150 days from issuance of this document

policy_statements.source_text: Send a written exception request for additional compliance time signed by the Agency Chief Information Officer with an Action Plan to mitigate standards not in compliance, milestones to accomplish mitigation efforts and timeframes for completion or an action plan and timeframe to achieve compliance with all the physical security requirements in this document; and
policy_statements.target: written exception request for additional compliance time signed by the Agency Chief Information Officer

policy_statements.source_text: Include these requirements in all Statements of Work (SOW) and Procurement Requests for IT Restricted Space until there is a permanent revision of the FAR.
policy_statements.target: all Statements of Work (SOW) and Procurement Requests for IT Restricted Space
conditions: until there is a permanent revision of the FAR

policy_statements.source_text: Agency Managers for IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Web Farms, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) and Isolation Zones will:
Ensure that facilities under their control comply with all physical security requirements outlined in this manual;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Managers for IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Web Farms, Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIF) and Isolation Zones

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with agency CIO and ISSPM for each location/facility that does not meet these requirements to prepare a exception request package; this request will include an Action Plan to mitigate standards not in compliance, milestones to accomplish mitigation efforts and timeframes for completion or an action plan and timeframe to achieve compliance with the physical security requirements in this document;

The United States Department of Agriculture houses and processes information relating to the privacy of US citizens, payroll and financial transactions, proprietary information and life/mission critical data.
information relating to the privacy of US citizens, payroll and financial transactions, proprietary information and life/mission critical data
It is essential that this information be protected from the risk and magnitude of loss or harm that could result from inadvertent or deliberate disclosure, alteration or destruction.
USDA must protect information resources through layered physical security, high logical data security and effective security procedures and administration.
Successful IT security protection dictates the physical control of restricted space that contains major USDA computer and telecommunications resources.
physical control of restricted space that contains major USDA computer and telecommunications resources
The purpose of this chapter is to define the physical security standards for all IT equipment/devices in this space.
physical security standards for all IT equipment/devices in this space
Many USDA facilities house highly sensitive critical IT infrastructure components.
highly sensitive critical IT infrastructure components
As such, it is essential that every precaution be used to safeguard this information capability.
Information technology infrastructures will be housed in IT Restricted Space that meets the requirements of the physical security standards outlined below.
that meets the requirements of the physical security standards outlined below
All USDA agencies are responsible for coordinating the physical security requirements of their critical infrastructure resources.
physical security requirements of their critical infrastructure resources

Specifically, agencies are responsible for coordinating the physical security requirements of all IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Telecommunications/Local Area Network (LAN) Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones.
physical security requirements of all IT Restricted Space that includes Computer Facilities, Telecommunications/Local Area Network (LAN) Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones
These standards apply to existing and planned space to be utilized for this purpose.
existing and planned space to be utilized for this purpose
to be utilized for this purpose

While every IT facility may not meet the physical security standards outlined above, CS will work with the agency, functional business owner and others to develop acceptable short and long term mitigation strategies to meet the needs of the Department.
acceptable short and long term mitigation strategies
While every IT facility may not meet the physical security standards outlined above
IT Restricted Space will be controlled directly by USDA personnel who will have the ultimate responsibility for control of these areas.

New or planned specifications for IT Restricted Space will contain a provision that the physical security requirements will be coordinated with Cyber Security far enough in advance during the design phase to ensure compliance with this policy.
New or planned specifications for IT Restricted Space

Pending revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) to include security requirements, all agencies will include physical security requirements in all Statements of Work (SOW) and Procurement Requests for IT Restricted Space.
Pending revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) to include security requirements
Agencies will submit all policy exception requests directly to the ACIO for Cyber Security.
Exceptions to policy will be considered only in terms of implementation timeframes; exceptions will not be granted to the requirement to conform to this policy.
only in terms of implementation timeframes

Exceptions that are approved will be interim in nature and will require that each agency report this Granted Policy Exception (GPE) as a Plan of Action & Milestone (POA&M) in their FISMA reporting, with a GPE notation, until full compliance is achieved.
Interim exceptions expire with each fiscal year.
Compliance exceptions that require longer durations will be renewed on an annual basis with a updated timeline for completion.
Compliance exceptions that require longer durations
on an annual basis with a updated timeline for completion
CS will monitor all approved exceptions.
The Critical Infrastructure consists of those physical and cyber-based systems essential to the minimum operations of the economy and government.
They include, but are not limited to, telecommunications, energy, banking and finance, transportation, water systems and emergency services, both governmental and private.
Many of the nation’s critical infrastructures have been physically and logically separate systems that have little interdependence.
This is also true in the case of USDA’s Critical Infrastructure, which is managed collectively under different programs in the department.
The goals of these programs are diverse and not always overlapping in their security efforts.

USDA buildings that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment automatically are considered critical IT Infrastructure Restricted Space and USDA must provide a level of physical security commensurate with that designation.
USDA buildings that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment
that house Computing Facilities, Telecommunications/LAN Rooms, Web Farms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones equipment
Devices, in these facilities, which process or access sensitive data on a recurring basis will be protected in accordance with minimum security protection standards.
which process or access sensitive data on a recurring basis
IT Restricted Space areas must be secured in accordance with the requirements specified below:

Physical security for this space will be provided in compliance with the recommendations established for Federal Facilities by the Department of Justice, Vulnerability Assessment, dated June 28, 1995.
Department of Justice, Vulnerability Assessment, dated June 28, 1995
Parking : Facility parking will be controlled; signs will be posted and arrangements will be made for towing of unauthorized vehicles; adequate lighting will be provided for parking areas;
Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) : CCTV surveillance cameras with time-lapse video recording will be provided;
CCTV surveillance cameras with time-lapse video recording
Lighting : Lighting with emergency power backup will be provided;
Access Control : Facility will be controlled by armed security guards and an intrusion detection system with central monitoring capability maintained to current life safety standards;
Entrances/Exits : High security locks will be installed and used;
Employee/Visitor Identification : Agency photo ID will be required for all personnel and ID will be displayed at all times; visitors will be controlled and screened;
Utilities : Utility access will be restricted to authorized personnel; emergency power will be provided to all critical systems (alarms, radio communications, computer facilities, etc.);
Occupant Emergency Plans (OEP) : OEPs will be implemented in facilities, updated and tested annually;
Training : Annual Security Awareness Training will be conducted.
Prior to the determination of a IT Restricted Space location, consideration will be given to its proximity to public areas.
Prior to the determination of a IT Restricted Space location
Public areas are defined as areas that are maintained for or can be used by the public or the general community, such as rest rooms, libraries or visitor centers.
should not be located either above, adjacent, or below public areas in multi-story buildings;
All packages being delivered to the IT Restricted Space will be x-rayed first.
All packages being delivered to the IT Restricted Space
All mail/packages must be recorded in a log book;

Periodic inspections of the door locking mechanism will be conducted by agency IT personnel on a bi-annual basis to provide assurance that hardware cannot be easily manipulated to gain unauthorized access;
Periodic inspections of the door locking mechanism
The roving guard will periodically inspect IT Restricted Space entrances for signs of forced entry; and
Signage indicating IT Restricted Space locations is prohibited.
Signage indicating IT Restricted Space locations
Physical Security Standards for IT Restricted Space  -
The IT Restricted Space will be located in the interior of the building away from exterior windows, if practical;
If floor plans are used at entrances to identify locations within the facility, critical asset locations will not be identified;
If floor plans are used at entrances to identify locations within the facility
Wall construction of the IT Restricted Space will be slab-to-slab with Sound Transmission Class 40 or better and other criteria cited in the ISC Security Design Criteria for Federal Buildings;
Wall construction of the IT Restricted Space
ISC Security Design Criteria for Federal Buildings
The computer room will be protected by a fire suppressant system in accordance with local fire code, preferably dry-pipe;
Entrances to the IT Restricted Space will be kept to the minimum required by local fire code;
Entrances to the IT Restricted Space
Activities with visitor populations will be located a minimum of 50 feet from IT Restricted Space ;
Mailrooms will not be located within 50 feet of IT Restricted Space and cannot be placed over or under this space;
Storage areas and loading docks will not be located within 50 feet of IT Restricted Space and cannot be placed over or under this space;
Glass doors or windows will not be used in IT Restricted Space;
Metal clad doors or solid wood doors with a 2-hour fire rating will be used at all IT Restricted Space entrances;
Metal clad doors or solid wood doors with a 2-hour fire rating
Entrance to the computer room will be via electronic access control with the capability of providing an audit trail; Biometric Systems are encouraged;
Exterior computer room doors having key access hardware will be removed from the Master Key system of the facility;
Exterior computer room doors having key access hardware
The issuance of non-Master Keys must be controlled only to individuals with an ongoing business need;
only to individuals with an ongoing business need
An intrusion detection system will be installed on all computer room entrances;
The access control and intrusion detection systems will have Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) backup;
access control and intrusion detection systems
Exterior IT Restricted Space doors will have either interior hinges or exterior hinges with non-removable pins;
Based on the determination of mission criticality by each agency, computer rooms and web farms will have back-up generators and UPS;
Based on the determination of mission criticality by each agency
Weapons are not allowed in IT Restricted space with the exception of armed security officers, law enforcement and other investigative personnel; and
with the exception of armed security officers, law enforcement and other investigative personnel
Backup tapes that contain mission critical or sensitive information will be stored offsite.
Backup tapes that contain mission critical or sensitive information
that contain mission critical or sensitive information
Only personnel having an ongoing recurring business need will be given unescorted access to the IT Restricted Space;
personnel having an ongoing recurring business need
having an ongoing recurring business need
Personnel who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space will immediately be removed from the access control system;
Personnel who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space
who no longer have a business need to enter Restricted Space
Visitors should be kept to a bare minimum; tours by non-USDA personnel are prohibited;

A sign in/sign out logbook shall be required for all escorted visitors; as a minimum the logbook shall contain the printed identity of each visitor, visitor’s signature, agency/company represented, purpose of visit, date/time in and date/time out;
Cleaning and maintenance personnel shall be escorted at all times by USDA or permanent contractor personnel;
An individual who has knowledge of the system being worked on shall escort non-permanent contractors needing access to the IT Restricted Space at all times; and

Promote and support effective physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space.

The Associate CIO for Cyber Security will:

Publish physical security standards for all USDA Information Technology (IT) Restricted Space, to include Computer Facilities, Web Farms, Telecommunications/Magnetic Media Rooms, SCIFs and Isolation Zones ;

Actively participate in the planning and design of all new IT Restricted Space to ensure that IT physical security standards are incorporated in space layouts for offices, buildings and complexes;

Conduct on-site reviews of all existing IT Restricted Space to ensure that all Mission Critical, Departmental Priority and Sensitive Systems are protected through adequate layered physical security;
Provide subject matter expert advice to USDA agencies on physical security standards as they relate to IT Restricted Space; and
Review all exception requests concerning compliance time limit extensions or alternate methods of mitigating physical security risks by USDA agencies as they relate to IT Restricted Space.
